passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
David was the author.
This is a song or poem.
This psalm is for worship.

passages.text: O LORD, who may abide in Your tent? Who may dwell on Your holy mountain?
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He speaks to the LORD.
He asks a question.
He says, “O LORD, who may live in Your tent?”
He also asks, “Who may stay on Your holy mountain?”
passages.original: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָ֫וִ֥ד יְ֭הֹוָה מִי־ יָג֣וּר בְּאָהֳלֶ֑ךָ מִֽי־ יִ֝שְׁכֹּ֗ן בְּהַ֣ר קָדְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: He who walks with integrity and practices righteousness, who speaks the truth from his heart, who has no slander on his tongue, who does no harm to his neighbor, who casts no scorn on his friend, who despises the vile but honors those who fear the LORD, who does not revise a costly oath, who lends his money without interest and refuses a bribe against the innocent. He who does these things will never be shaken.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He describes the person who may live with God.
This person walks with integrity.
He does what is right.
He speaks the truth from his heart.
He does not slander with his tongue.
He does not harm his neighbor.
He does not bring shame on his friend.
He despises those who do evil.
He honors those who fear the LORD.
He keeps his promises, even when it is hard.
He does not lend his money for interest.
He does not take a bribe against the innocent.
Whoever does these things will never be shaken.
passages.original: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים וּפֹעֵ֥ל צֶ֑דֶק וְדֹבֵ֥ר אֱ֝מֶ֗ת בִּלְבָבֽוֹ׃ לֹֽא־ רָגַ֨ל׀ עַל־ לְשֹׁנ֗וֹ לֹא־ עָשָׂ֣ה לְרֵעֵ֣הוּ רָעָ֑ה וְ֝חֶרְפָּ֗ה לֹא־ נָשָׂ֥א עַל־ קְרֹֽבוֹ׃ נִבְזֶ֤ה׀ בְּֽעֵ֘ינָ֤יו נִמְאָ֗ס וְאֶת־ יִרְאֵ֣י יְהוָ֣ה יְכַבֵּ֑ד נִשְׁבַּ֥ע לְ֝הָרַ֗ע וְלֹ֣א יָמִֽר׃ כַּסְפּ֤וֹ׀ לֹא־ נָתַ֣ן בְּנֶשֶׁךְ֮ וְשֹׁ֥חַד עַל־ נָקִ֗י לֹ֥א לָ֫קָ֥ח עֹֽשֵׂה־ אֵ֑לֶּה לֹ֖א יִמּ֣וֹט לְעוֹלָֽם׃
